identity.title: RIPK4 links NF-kappaB-associated signaling and VEGF production to melanoma-endothelial communication.

content.abstract: PURPOSE: Melanoma progression is driven by aberrant intracellular signaling and reciprocal communication with the tumor microenvironment. Although receptor-interacting protein kinase 4 (RIPK4) has been implicated in melanoma progression, its role in tumor-endothelial communication remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the contribution of RIPK4 to melanoma-endothelial communication, focusing on its association with NF-kappaB signaling and VEGFA expression, and their role in melanoma-derived paracrine activation of endothelial cells. METHODS: CRISPR/Cas9-edited A375 RIPK4 knockout (A375 (RIPK4.KO)) and WM266.4 RIPK4-deficient (WM266.4(RIPK4.KO)) melanoma cells, together with their respective controls, were analyzed in two- and three-dimensional culture models. VEGFA expression and secretion, NF-kappaB-associated signaling, and RIPK4-associated changes in the melanoma secretome were assessed by qPCR, ELISA, Western blotting, and angiogenesis protein arrays. The functional consequences were evaluated using conditioned media in human aortic endothelial cell tube formation assays and the chick chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model. RESULTS: RIPK4 depletion was associated with reduced p65 phosphorylation and increased IkappaBalpha expression, accompanied by decreased VEGFA expression and VEGF secretion. Restoration of RIPK4 reversed these changes, restoring p65 phosphorylation, reducing IkappaBalpha expression, and increasing VEGF levels. Secretome profiling revealed reduced VEGF and amphiregulin and increased pigment epithelium-derived factor following RIPK4 depletion. Conditioned media from RIPK4-deficient cells impaired endothelial tube formation, which was restored by recombinant VEGF165. In CAM, RIPK4 depletion reduced CD34 and VEGFR3 (FLT4), without significantly affecting overall vascularization. CONCLUSION: RIPK4 is associated with NF-kappaB signaling and VEGF production in melanoma cells and contributes to the regulation of the melanoma secretome and melanoma-endothelial communication. These findings support a role for RIPK4 in modulating paracrine signals that influence endothelial cell behavior, although the direct mechanistic contribution of NF-kappaB to RIPK4-mediated VEGFA regulation remains to be established.
